ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there are upper and lower common wires serving as the same pair of nodes. Resistor R1 is vertically connected between the upper and lower nodes, and resistor R2 is also vertically connected between the same upper and lower nodes; therefore R1 and R2 are in a parallel relationship. The total current I enters the upper node from the left along the upper wire and splits at that node, where I1 flows downward through R1 and I2 flows downward through R2. Reasoning: Since R1 and R2 are in parallel, the voltages across their two ends are the same; let this common voltage be V. By Ohm's law, the current flowing through R1 is I1 = V/R1, and the current flowing through R2 is I2 = V/R2. The total current I = I1 + I2 = V/R1 + V/R2. Thus I1/I = (V/R1)/(V/R1 + V/R2). Simplifying gives I1/I = R2/(R1 + R2), so I1 = [R2/(R1 + R2)] I.
